name: Archaic Greeks
place: the city-states of Greece and the Aegean
desc: Hundreds of small, quarrelsome city-states sharing one language and one set of gods, who borrowed the Phoenician letters and added vowels, held games at Olympia, sent colonies from Spain to the Black Sea, and began to ask what the world is made of.
source: Homer and Hesiod; Herodotus; inscriptions and excavations at Olympia, Delphi, Athens and Samos

belligerent: held the line in the phalanx while the shield beside me shook
devout: walked to Delphi to ask the god a question, and puzzled over the answer for a year
cautious: asked what everything is made of, and could not stop asking

inventions.name: Letters with Vowels
inventions.source: Around 800 BCE the Greeks adapted the Phoenician alphabet and used spare letters for vowels, creating the first full alphabet
inventions.desc: Every sound written, consonant and vowel, so a poem can be read exactly as it was sung: the tribe gathers much more lore.

inventions.name: Hoplite Phalanx
inventions.source: From the 7th century BCE citizens fought shoulder to shoulder, each round shield covering the man to his left
inventions.desc: A wall of bronze shields and spears, each man trusting his neighbour: +2 defence, +1 attack.
inventions.hint: Needs Bronze Metallurgy, and fighters who train together.

inventions.name: Medicine Without Gods
inventions.source: The Hippocratic writings (5th century BCE) explained illness by natural causes, with careful notes of each case
inventions.desc: Watch the patient, write down what you see, and help nature heal: the sick recover 20% faster, the hurt heal 10% faster.
inventions.hint: Needs willow bark and the Tribe & Agrarian Era.

inventions.name: The Theatre
inventions.source: Drama grew out of choruses for Dionysus; Thespis is said to have been the first actor, in Athens around 534 BCE
inventions.desc: A hillside of seats around a round dancing floor, where the whole town laughs and weeps together: +4 mood.
inventions.hint: Needs the Tribe & Agrarian Era, and songs at the rites.

inventions.name: Tunnel Through the Mountain
inventions.source: The tunnel of Eupalinos on Samos (6th century BCE), over 1 km long, was dug from both ends at once and met in the middle
inventions.desc: A water tunnel dug from both sides of a hill by geometry alone: farm plots yield 15% more, +1 mood.
inventions.hint: Needs Polished Stone Tools and the Bronze & Mythic Era.

foods.name: Barley Cake and Olive Oil
foods.desc: Maza, kneaded barley meal, eaten with oil, olives and figs: hunger grows 10% slower.

foods.name: Mixed Wine
foods.source: Greeks drank wine mixed with water in a great bowl, the krater; drinking it neat was thought barbarous
foods.desc: Wine mixed with water in a painted bowl, shared with songs and arguments: +3 mood.

finds.name: Thyme Hives
finds.source: The thyme honey of Mount Hymettus near Athens was praised throughout antiquity
finds.desc: Wild bees in the thyme of the hills, with honey that smells of the mountain. Once known, +1 mood.

finds.name: Olive Groves
finds.desc: The goddess's gift to her city: the olive tree, food, light and medicine at once.

people.name: Kleobis
people.desc: He won the foot race and never lets anyone forget it.
memory: won the stadion race and was crowned with olive

people.name: Hipparchia
people.desc: She asks questions until the elders run out of answers.
memory: argued all night at the symposium about whether the soul is fire or air

people.name: Homer
people.source: The Iliad and the Odyssey, set down around the 8th–7th century BCE
people.desc: The poet to whom the Greeks gave their two great epics; whether he was one man, many, or none is still argued.

people.name: Thales
people.desc: The first to ask what everything is made of (water, he said), who is said to have predicted the eclipse of 585 BCE.

people.name: Sappho
people.source: Fragments of her poems, from papyri and later quotations
people.desc: A poet of Lesbos whose songs of love and longing survive only in fragments; Plato called her the tenth Muse.

people.name: Herodotus
people.source: His Histories, written in the 5th century BCE
people.text: a curious traveller who asks everyone about their customs, gods and grandparents, and writes it all down.
memory: travelled from Egypt to Babylon asking questions
people.desc: The 'father of history', whose stories of distant peoples fill this game.

people.name: Leonidas
people.label: Leonidas of the Narrow Pass
people.desc: A king who holds a pass against an empire. Combat 9, Defence.

people.name: Pythagoras
people.label: Pythagoras, who Heard Numbers
people.desc: He hears the harmony of numbers in the lyre and the stars. Lore 7, Crafting 6.

events.title: Games at the Sanctuary
events.source: The Olympic Games, traditionally first held in 776 BCE; a sacred truce let athletes travel safely
events.text: Neighbouring villages propose a truce and a festival of games for the gods: races, wrestling, the javelin. The winners would be crowned with olive and remembered forever.

options.label: Hold the games
options.result: For five days no one fights. Our runner wins, and the olive crown hangs in the hut for good.

options.label: No time for games
options.result: The others hold their games without us.

events.title: Write a Name on a Potsherd
events.source: Athenian ostracism (from c. 487 BCE): citizens scratched a name on a potsherd, and the man with most votes was exiled for ten years
events.text: One leader has grown so powerful that people fear he will make himself king. Someone suggests a vote: everyone scratches a name on a broken pot, and whoever gets the most must leave for ten years.

options.label: Hold the vote
options.result: The potsherds are counted. The powerful man leaves, furious, and the assembly feels a little braver.

events.title: A New City Over the Sea
events.source: Greek cities sent out colonies from Marseille to the Crimea; the founder (oikistes) often first asked the oracle at Delphi
events.text: There are too many mouths and too little land. The oracle says: go west, over the sea, where a river meets a hill. Who will go?

options.label: Send settlers with the sacred fire

do.feat: Sent settlers to found a city over the sea

options.result: Ships leave with fire from the home hearth. A year later the first gifts come back from the new city.

options.label: Make do with the land we have
options.result: The fields are divided again, smaller.

tales.name: Prometheus Steals Fire
tales.source: Hesiod, Theogony and Works and Days
tales.text: The king of the gods hid fire from people. But the Titan Prometheus, who loved them, stole a spark from heaven in a hollow fennel stalk and brought it down to earth. For that he was chained to a mountain, where an eagle eats his liver every day.

tales.name: Demeter and Persephone
tales.text: The lord of the dead carried off the grain goddess's daughter. In her grief Demeter let nothing grow. At last the girl was found, but because she had eaten six seeds of a pomegranate below, she must spend part of every year there. While she is gone, her mother mourns, and that is winter.
tales.moral: what is lost returns with the spring

tales.name: The Ant and the Grasshopper
tales.text: All summer the grasshopper sang while the ant carried grain to her nest. When winter came, the grasshopper, starving, begged the ant for food. 'You sang all summer,' said the ant. 'Now you can dance all winter.'

tales.name: The Festival of Dionysus
tales.source: The City Dionysia at Athens, where tragedies and comedies were staged in competition
tales.text: In spring the god of wine comes back to the city. His statue is carried in, a bull is sacrificed, and for days the whole town sits on the hillside watching masked actors and singing choruses tell the old stories, until the judges name the best.
tales.moral: the city that laughs and weeps together stays together
